source.title: CBSE Sample Question Paper 2025-26, Physics (042), Class XII
source.subject: physics
source.notes: Paper prints: 33 questions in all, Maximum Marks 70, Time Allowed 3 hours. Five sections: A (Q1-16, 1 mark each: 12 MCQ + 4 assertion-reason), B (Q17-21, 2 marks each, internal choice in Q20 and Q21), C (Q22-28, 3 marks each, internal choice in Q27), D (Q29-30, two case-study questions of 4 marks each), E (Q31-33, 5 marks each, all three with internal choice). English-only paper (no Hindi text observed). "For Visually Impaired candidates" alternative sub-questions are printed for Q5, Q6, Q7, Q18, Q20(II), Q26, Q30(II) and Q30(III); these alternatives were skipped per instructions and are not included as separate entries. Q32's two OR alternatives were printed by the source PDF as interleaved lines across a two-column layout (label "32(II)" appearing before the second line of alternative (I)'s own sub-part (B)); the sub-part grouping used here — 32(I) = lens-maker derivation + equi-convex radius calculation (3+2 marks), 32(II) = angle-of-deviation definition + prism relation derivation + minimum-deviation condition (1+3+1 marks) — was reconstructed from reading order and cross-checked against the marking scheme's own grouping. Several apparent errors/inconsistencies in the source PDFs are reproduced verbatim rather than corrected, and flagged per-question: the marking scheme for Q32(I)(B) calls the lens "convexo-concave" although the question asks about an "Equi-convex" lens; the marking scheme for Q31(II)(B) explains a work-done-along-two-paths answer using "electric field is conservative" although the question states "uniform external magnetic field"; the marking scheme for Q33(I)(C) mentions "Rv... parallel" although only an ammeter (Ra) conversion was asked; the marking scheme text for Q28's and Q29(II)/(III)/(IV)'s final numeric steps contains garbled stacked-fraction fragments that could not be reliably reconstructed. Exponents written inline in the source as e.g. "x10-7" (meaning x10⁻⁷) are kept exactly as printed rather than converted to unicode superscripts, since this is the paper's own plain-text convention throughout (including the physical-constants list) and is unambiguous. Vertically stacked fractions split across lines by the extractor were rebuilt inline as "numerator/denominator" and flagged per question. Nuclear isotope notation (mass number/atomic number as super/subscripts, e.g. ²³⁹₉₄Pu) is flattened in the extracted text of Q24 and flagged.

questions.text: If a charged hollow sphere and a solid sphere of aluminum and copper of equal radii are in electrostatic equilibrium, then which of the following statements is true?
options: Both the spheres are having equal charges.
The hollow sphere will have more charge than solid sphere at its surface.
The aluminum sphere will have more charge on its surface than copper sphere.
If hollow sphere is also made up of aluminum then it will have more charge.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fraction V = q/C in the official answer); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: (A) / Both are having equal charges. For two bodies to be in equilibrium, both should have same potential (V). As V = q/C, where C of sphere is 4πε₀r, which is independent of all the factors mentioned in options.

questions.text: A coil contains N turns of insulated copper wire of diameter d and resistivity ρ wound on a cylinder of diameter D. What is the total resistance between the two ends of the coil of copper wire? (given: D>>d)
options: 4ρND/d²
8ρND/d²
2ρND/d²
12ρND/d²
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/powers in the options and the official answer, e.g. 4ρND/d²); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: (A) / Diameter of copper wire d, diameter of cylindrical iron is D, no. of turns N, (D>>d). Length = N x Circumference of cylinder. L = NπD. R = ρL/A = ρNπD/(πd²/4) = 4ρND/d².

questions.text: If the phasor diagram for a device connected to AC supply is as shown in the fig, then which of the following statements is true?
options: When the frequency of the AC source is increased than the impedance of the device decreases.
This device behaves as conducting wire when connected across DC source.
When the frequency of the AC source is decreased than the impedance of the device decreases.
This device stores energy in the form of magnetic potential energy.

officialAnswer.text: (A) / When the frequency of the AC source is increased than the impedance of the device decreases. As in phasor diagram current leads the voltage, so given appliance is capacitor.

figures.alt: Phasor diagram with phasors V and I on x-y axes

questions.text: Which of the following statement is true for the radio waves and the gamma rays?
options: The energy of gamma rays is lesser than that of the radio waves.
The frequency of the radio waves is higher than that of gamma rays.
The radio waves and the gamma rays have the same energy.
The energy of radio waves is lesser than that of the gamma rays.

officialAnswer.text: (D) / The energy of radio waves is lesser than that of the gamma rays. Since the frequency of radio waves is less than gamma waves. E = hν. Hence, energy of radio waves is less than gamma waves.

questions.text: Which of the following transitions corresponds to the emission of the radiation of the maximum wavelength?
options: I
III
IV
VI
extractionIssues: Subscripts flattened: ΔE_I, ΔE_II, ΔE_IV

officialAnswer.text: (C) / IV. Transition III, V, VI corresponds to absorption of energy. Maximum emitted wavelength corresponds minimum energy difference. ΔE_I > ΔE_II > ΔE_IV. Therefore, maximum emitted wavelength corresponds to transition IV.

questions.text: A charged particle is projected along the axis of a current carrying loop. Which of the following statements is true?
options: The acceleration of the charged particle will depend on the velocity with which it is projected.
The acceleration of the charged particle will depend on the magnitude of the current passing through the coil.
The acceleration of the charged particle will depend on the radius of the coil.
The charged particle will move with constant velocity.

officialAnswer.text: (D) / The charged particle will move with constant velocity. As charge particle is moving parallel to magnetic field, there will be no acceleration.

questions.text: Two small identical magnets are allowed to fall freely one through a vertical solenoid of 20 m made up of copper and another in air through the same vertical distance. The time taken by the two magnets to fall will be
options: same in both the cases.
more for the magnet falling in air.
more for the magnet falling through the solenoid.
infinite.

officialAnswer.text: (C) / more for the magnet falling through the solenoid. Emf will be induced in solenoid due to motion of magnet through it. As per Lenz's law induced emf will oppose the motion of magnet.

questions.text: The emf generated by an AC generator is given by V=Vo sin ωt, where ω is angular frequency of armature of generator. What will be the emf if the angular frequency is doubled?
options: V=Vo sin 2ωt
V=2Vo sin ωt
V=2Vo sin 2ωt
V=Vo sin ωt

officialAnswer.text: (C) / V=2Vo sin 2ωt. As V = NBAω sin ωt.

questions.text: When we move magnetic compass from point P to Q then which of the following statement is true?
options: The deflection of the magnetic needle at P and Q will be in the same direction.
The deflection of the magnetic needle at P and Q will be in the opposite directions.
The deflection of the magnetic needle at P and Q will be perpendicular to each other.
The deflection of the magnetic needle at P and Q will be inclined at 45° with respect to each other.

officialAnswer.text: (B) / The deflection of the magnetic needle at P and Q will be in the opposite directions. As magnetic field at equator is antiparallel to magnetic field at pole.

questions.text: The amplitude of the magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave propagating along positive X axis in vacuum is 510 nT k̂ and its angular frequency is 60 x 10⁶ rad/sec. Write the expression for the electric field (E⃗).

officialAnswer.text: Given, B₀ = 510 nT = 510 x 10⁻⁹ T, ω = 60 x 10⁶ rad/sec. E₀ = cB₀ = 153 N/C. k = ω/c = 20 x 10⁻² rad/m. E = E₀ sin (ωt – kz). E = 153 sin (60 x 10⁶ t – 20 x10⁻²x) N/C.

questions.text:
The following graph shows the potential difference across the terminals of a cell against its load current. Find,
(I) the emf of the cell and
(II) the internal resistance of the cell.
extractionIssues: For Visually Impaired candidates an alternative version of this question ('find the relation between internal resistance, emf, external resistance and total current') is printed on page 7; that alternative was not extracted, per instructions

officialAnswer.text: (I) E.m.f of the cell is 6V, as when load current is zero potential difference becomes equal to emf of the cell. (II) The internal resistance of a cell can be determined as the negative slope of its voltage-current graph. First, we can determine the slope by choosing two points on the line: Slope = (0-6)/(12-0) = -0.5. This means that the internal resistance must be 0.50 ohm (Ω).

figures.alt: Graph of potential difference / V against load current / A showing a straight line

questions.text: A charge q is placed inside a sphere of radius 'a' filled with water and another charge 2q is placed inside cube of side '2a' which is vacuumed inside. Find the ratio of the flux linked with the sphere to that linked with the cube. (Take relative permittivity of water as 80)
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: From Gauss's theorem, Φ = q/(εrε₀) [where εr is relative permittivity of medium inside Gaussian surface]. For sphere, Φsphere = q/(εwaterε₀) …(i). For cube, Φcube = 2q/ε₀ …(ii). Dividing (i) by (ii): Φsphere/Φcube = 1/(2εwater) = 1/160.

questions.text: Write an expression for the magnetic force per unit length between two parallel thin current carrying wires. Hence define one ampere.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fraction F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/2πr); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: F/L = μ₀I₁I₂/(2πr) (I₁ is the current in first wire and I₂ is the current in second wire). Thus we define ampere as the current flowing in each conductor separated by a unit distance so that one conductor applies a force of 2 x 10⁻⁷ N on a unit length of another parallel conductor.

questions.text: How does the impact parameter affect the trajectory of a α-particles scattered by a heavy nucleus? What is the value of impact parameter for head on collision of α-particles with the nucleus?

officialAnswer.text: Smaller is the impact parameter, larger is the angle at which α-particles scatters. Larger is the impact parameter, α-particles scatter less keeping its original trajectory. For head on collision, the value of impact parameter is zero.

questions.text: Plot a graph showing variation of de-Broglie wavelength λ versus 1/√V, where V is accelerating potential for a particle of mass m and charge q. Obtain the slope of this graph.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions/roots); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: λ = h/(mv). λ = h/√(2mqV), comparing this equation with y = mx. Slope = h/√(2mq).

questions.text: With the help of circuit diagram explain working of the full wave rectifier.
extractionIssues: Answer diagram (full-wave rectifier circuit and output waveform) referenced in the marking scheme is not reproduced

officialAnswer.text: In the full wave rectifier: D1 and D2 are pn junction diode which allow current to pass only in forward biasing. During odd half cycle the diode D1 will be forward biased hence potential at the Q will be more than potential at P and during this cycle D2 will not permit current through it. During even half cycle the diode D2 will be forward biased hence potential at the Q will be more than potential at P and during this cycle D1 will not permit current through it. Hence we will get DC as output as shown in diagram.

questions.text:
A compound microscope consists of an objective lens of focal length 0.82 cm and an eyepiece lens of focal length 2.9 cm. An object is placed 0.91 cm from the objective lens. The image is formed at the near point (25 cm) from the eye.
(I) Calculate that the angular magnification of the microscope.
(II) Draw the ray diagram of compound microscope in normal adjustment.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions); check against the PDF
Official answer for (II) is a ray diagram and is not in the text layer

officialAnswer.text: (I) 1/v₀ = 1/f₀ − 1/u₀. v₀ = 8.3 cm. Angular magnification M = m₀ x mₑ = (v₀/u₀) x (D/fₑ + 1). M = -(8.3/0.91) x (25/2.9 + 1). M = -87.7.

questions.text: Draw the reflected wave front for a plane wave front incident on a plane reflecting surface. Hence verify the laws of reflection using Huygen's principle.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions with denominator c); check against the PDF
Diagram (incident and reflected wavefronts with points A-G) referenced in the marking scheme is not reproduced
For VI Candidates an alternative text-only version of this question (define wavefront/wavelet/shape of the wavefront) is printed on page 8; that alternative was not extracted, per instructions

officialAnswer.text: If c be the speed of light, t be the time taken by light to go from B to C or A to D or E to G through F, then t = (EF+FG)/c. t = (AF Sin i)/c + (FC Sin r)/c. t = (AC Sin r + AF(Sin i − Sin r))/c. For rays of light from different parts on the incident wavefront, the values of AF are different. But light from different points of the incident wavefront should take the same time to reach the corresponding points on the reflected wavefront. So, t should not depend upon AF. This is possible only if sin i – sin r = 0, i.e. sin i = sin r or i = r. Hence proved.

questions.text:
If a point sized object having charge 1C and mass 1g is projected with velocity of 2î m/s from a point (0,2cm,0) in the region of magnetic field -0.1k̂ T which spreads in the first quadrant.
(A) What will be the shape of the path followed by the given charged particle?
(B) At what point it will cross the X-axis?
(C) What will be the kinetic energy of particle when it will enter in the fourth quadrant?
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fraction R = mv/qB); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: As the charged particle is moving perpendicular to the magnetic field it will follow circular trajectory in clockwise direction. Magnetic force will act as centripetal force. Given: Q=1C; M=10⁻³kg; v=2m/s & B=-0.1T k̂. Radius of trajectory is given by R = mv/(qB) = 2cm. (A) Quarter Circle. (B) It will cross the X axis at 2cm. (C) As work done by B on the charge particle is zero, its kinetic energy (K) will remain same. K = ½mv². Or, K = ½ x 10⁻³ x 2² J = 2 x 10⁻³ J.

questions.text:
A solenoid has a core of material with relative permeability 200. The windings of the solenoid are insulated from the core and carry a current of 1A. If the number of turns is 2000 per metre, calculate
(A) magnetic intensity,
(B) magnetic field &
(C) magnetisation

officialAnswer.text: Given: μr=200, I=1A, N=2000turn/m. (A) H = nI = 2000/m x 1A = 2 x 10³ A/m. (B) B = μ₀μrH = 200 x 4π x 10⁻⁷ x 2 x 10³ A/m = 0.50 T. (C) Magnetisation is given by M = (μr - 1)H = 199 x 10³ A/m = 1.99 x 10⁵ A/m.

questions.text: A conducting coil of 50 turns and area 5/π cm² is rotating along the axis of solenoid of length 50cm and 2000 turns, carrying current of 5 A. What will be the value of maximum emf generated?
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions in the derivation); check against the PDF
Official answer's final result ('Or, εmax = 2Mv') is garbled in the marking-scheme text layer (likely a unit/OCR artifact); kept verbatim as printed

officialAnswer.text: Given: No. of turns of coil Nc=50. Area of coil = 5/π cm² = 5/π x 10⁻⁴ m². For solenoid: Ns=2000, L=0.5m, n = N/L=4000 turns/m, I= 5A. Magnetic field due to solenoid B=μ₀nI. Or, B=4000 x 4π x 10⁻⁷ x 5 T. Or, B= 8π x 10⁻² T. Flux linked to coil ΦB=Nc B.A. Or, ΦB=NcBA cosωt. Emf ε = dΦB/dt = NcBAω sin ωt. Or, εmax = NcBA. Or, εmax = 50 x 8π x 10⁻² T x 5/π x 10⁻⁴m². Or, εmax = 2Mv.

questions.text:
Photoelectric effect is phenomenon of the ejection of electrons when the radiation of suitable frequency is made to fall on the surface of a metal. When light of suitable wavelength falls on the emitter C given in the diagram, the photoelectrons are emitted. These photoelectrons are drawn to the collector A. The photoelectric current of the order of a few microamperes can be normally obtained from the device given in figure. The device given converts a change in intensity of illumination into a change in photocurrent. This current can be used to operate control systems and in light measuring devices. The devices are made up of metals with low ionization enthalpies, for example platinum whose work function is 6.35 eV.

(I) If infrared radiation of 3 x 10¹¹ Hz is used as incident radiation, determine the reading of microammeter? Justify mathematically.
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fraction ν₀ = W₀/h); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: W₀ = hν₀. Threshold frequency, ν₀ = W₀/h = (6.35 x 1.6 x 10⁻¹⁹)/(6.63 x 10⁻³⁴) = 1.5 x 10¹⁵ Hz. Frequency of infrared radiation < threshold frequency (ν₀), hence no emission of photoelectrons will take place, therefore reading of the microammeter = 0.

questions.text:
(A) A dielectric slab of thickness t, is introduced between the plates of parallel plate capacitor of area A and separation d (where t<d). Find an expression for the capacitance with the dielectric slab.
(B) A copper sphere of capacitor C is dropped in ocean. Will the capacitance of the sphere increase, decrease or remain same? Justify.
(C) A capacitor is connected across a source of potential difference V and then the separation 'd' between the plates is increased using insulating stick. Plot 'V' vs 'd' graph for the given capacitor. (2+2+1)
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions, e.g. C = Aε₀/d, E = E₀/K); check against the PDF
Official answer for (C) is a V vs d graph and is not in the text layer
For VI Candidates an alternative version of part (C) ('will the energy stored in capacitor increase or decrease?') is printed on page 12; that alternative was not extracted, per instructions

officialAnswer.text: (A) In absence of dielectric slab, the capacitance of parallel plate capacitor is given by C = Aε₀/d. When a dielectric slab of thickness t (t<d) is introduced between the plates without touching the plates, the electric field in air E₀ = σ/ε₀ (σ is charge density given by q/A), but on account of polarisation of dielectric the electric field inside the dielectric changes to E = E₀/K. If potential difference between the plates of capacitor be V, then clearly V= E₀(d-t) + Et; Or, V= E₀(d-t) + E₀t/K; Or, V= E₀(d-t+t/K)= (σ/ε₀)(d-t+t/K); Or, V= (q/Aε₀)(d-t+t/K). (B) Capacitance of sphere will increase. Justification: As C=q/V & V=∫E.dl. As electric field will decrease, due to polarization of water, resulting in decrease in potential. Hence, capacitance of sphere will increase.

(B) If one charge particle is moved from A to C To B and another charge particle of equal magnitude is moved from A to D to B, In uniform external magnetic field. Than for which charge particle more work will be needed? (use fig for reference)

questions.text:
(A) Derive lens maker's formula.
(B) Equi-convex lenses are to be manufactured from a glass of refractive index 1.55, with both faces of the same radius of curvature. What is the radius of curvature required if the focal length is to be 10cm? (3+2)
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions throughout the lens-maker derivation); check against the PDF
The derivation uses point labels (P1, P2, N, O, I1, C, C1, C2, R1, R2) that assume a ray diagram not reproduced in the text layer
Sub-part order reconstructed from a two-column PDF layout on page 12 (the printed page interleaved the (I) and (II) alternatives' lines); grouping confirmed against the marking scheme
Marking scheme calls the lens 'convexo-concave' in part (B) although the question asks about an 'Equi-convex' lens; kept verbatim as printed (likely an inconsistency in the source)

officialAnswer.text: (A) Lens Maker's Formula: For refraction at LP1N, μ1/CO + μ2/CI1 = (μ2-μ1)/CC1 (as if the image is formed in the denser medium). For refraction at LP2N, μ2/(-CI1) + μ1/CI = (μ2-μ1)/CC2 (as if the object is in the denser medium and the image is formed in the rarer medium). Combining the refractions at both the surfaces: μ1/CO + μ2/CI = (μ2-μ1)(1/CC1 + 1/CC2). Substituting the values with sign conventions: -1/u + 1/v = ((μ2-μ1)/μ1)(1/R1 - 1/R2). Since μ2/μ1=μ: -1/u + 1/v = (μ-1)(1/R1 - 1/R2). When the object is kept at infinity, the image is formed at the principal focus, i.e. u = -∞, v = +f: 1/f = (μ-1)(1/R1 - 1/R2). This equation is called 'Lens Maker's Formula'. (B) Refractive index of glass, μ = 1.55. Focal length of the convexo-concave lens, f = 10 cm. Radius of curvature of one face of the first Convex surface = R1. Radius of curvature of the other face of the second convex surface = -R1. Therefore, R1 = R and R2 = -R. The value of R can be calculated from Lens-Maker formula: (1/f) = (μ - 1) [(1/R1) - (1/R2)]. (1/10) = (1.55 -1) [(1/R) + (1/R)]. (1/10) = 0.55 x (2/R). Therefore R = (0.55 x 2 x10) = 11cm. Hence, the radius of curvature of the convexo-concave is 11cm.

questions.text:
(A) Define angle of deviation in a prism?
(B) Obtain the relation A+δ=i+e for a prism where A is the angle of prism, δ is the angle of deviation, i is the angle of incidence and e is the angle of emergence. Write this relation for the minimum deviation?
(C) Write the condition for minimum deviation. (1+3+1)
extractionIssues: Sub-part order reconstructed from a two-column PDF layout on page 12 (the printed page interleaved the (I) and (II) alternatives' lines); grouping confirmed against the marking scheme
Diagram (prism construction APOQ with triangles OPQ and DPQ) referenced in the marking scheme is not reproduced

officialAnswer.text: (A) The angle of deviation represents the angle by which a light ray is deviated after passing through a prism. (B) Refraction of light through prism: In quadrilateral APOQ, A + O = 180° …(1). In triangle OPQ, r1 + r2 + O = 180° …(2). In triangle DPQ, δ = (i - r1) + (e - r2); δ = (i + e) – (r1 + r2) …(3). From (1) and (2), A = r1 + r2. From (3), δ = (i + e) – (A); i + e = A + δ. Sum of angle of incidence and angle of emergence is equal to the sum of angle of prism and angle of deviation. (C) When angle of incidence increases, the angle of deviation decreases. At a particular value of angle of incidence the angle of deviation becomes minimum and is called 'angle of minimum deviation'. At δm, i = e and r1 = r2 = r (say). At minimum deviation, refracted ray becomes parallel to incident ray. (Award full marks if either of condition is mentioned)

questions.text:
(A) State the working principle of a moving coil galvanometer? What modification is required in the galvanometer to make its scale linear?
(B) If a galvanometer of resistance 49.5Ω has range of 0.05A. What will be the value of resistance needed to convert it in ammeter of range 5A?
(C) How these two resistors should be connected to galvanometer in both cases? (2+2+1)
extractionIssues: Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fraction Ra = 0.5 x 49.5/4.95); check against the PDF
Official answer for (C) mentions 'Rv ... parallel' though only an ammeter conversion (Ra) was asked in (B); kept verbatim as printed (possibly a generic/reused marking-scheme answer)

officialAnswer.text: (A) Torque due to current carrying coil. Modification in designing of galvanometer are (i) Poles of magnet are made spherical (ii) Iron core is placed inside the coil. (B) Given: Rg =49.5Ω; Range=0.05A. For ammeter let resistance needed be Ra. As per requirement, Range x Rg =Ra(5-0.05). Ra = 0.5 x 49.5/4.95 = 0.5 Ω. (C) Ra will be connected in series & Rv is connected in parallel.

questions.text:
(A) An input potential Vin=200 Sin 100πt V is provided to an ideal transformer having 1000 turns in primary coil and 100 turns in secondary coil as shown in figure. The load circuit has a resistance of 4Ω, a capacitive reactance of 2Ω and an inductive reactance of 6Ω.
Find:
(i) the output voltage across the load circuit
(ii) the current flowing through the load circuit
(iii) the power supplied to the load circuit by the transformer
(B) State the working principle of a transformer and explain how it is a key component in the transfer of electrical power over long distances. (3+2)
extractionIssues: Circuit diagram ('as shown in figure') referenced in the question is not reproduced in the text layer
Notation rebuilt from the PDF layout (fractions and impedance formulas); check against the PDF

officialAnswer.text: Given: In load circuit, R=4Ω, Xc=2Ω, Xl=6Ω, Np=1000, Ns=100, Vin=200V sin100πt. (i) Output voltage across load circuit: Vout/Vin = Ns/Np = 0.1. Or, Vout=0.1 x 200V sin100πt. Or, Vout=20V sin100πt. (ii) Current flowing through load circuit: As, I=Im sin(ωt+ϕ), where Im= Vm/Z, Z=√(R² + (Xc-Xl)²). Or,Z=4√2 Ω. Im= 20/4√2 A = 5√2/2 A. ϕ = tan⁻¹((Xc-Xl)/R) = tan⁻¹(1) = π/4. I=5√2/2 A sin(100πt+π/4). (iii) Find the Power supplied to load circuit by the transformer: P= (VmIm/2)Cosϕ, where Cosϕ=cos(π/4) = 1/√2. P=20V x (5√2/2)A x 1/√2 =50W. (B) AC transformer works on the principal of 'Mutual Induction'. A.C. transformer can increase output potential. As P=V/I, so increase in output potential results in decrease in output current, resulting in significant decrease in power loss in transmission wires between power plants and cities. In respective cities they are stepped down.
